elements.element: Customer owns deliverables/work product created for it
elements.evidence: 14.2 "Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer"

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: 13.2 "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use ... embedded in a Deliverable"; 14.3 "the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies"

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: 14.1 "Customer owns all Customer Data ... No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process"
14.4 "No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument"

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: 14.3 "Vendor retains Vendor Technology"; Deliverable definition excludes "ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel"

elements.element: Customer receives perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence in deliverables (use, modify, sublicense)
elements.evidence: 14.2 (retained sentence) "Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term"; 13.2 grants only "permit contractors to support", no sublicensing of Deliverables

reasons: All six preferred atomic elements are now expressly present: Customer ownership plus a present assignment in 14.2, Vendor retention of Vendor Technology in 14.3, the perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free embedded-IP licence in 13.2 carried through by 14.3, Customer Data ownership in 14.1, and the no-joint-ownership rule in 14.4.
The edit is minimal in form — a single sentence replaced with an operator flip plus a short assignment phrase, no boilerplate added.

Intent is not preserved: the second sentence of 14.2 was left untouched, so Customer simultaneously 'exclusively owns every Deliverable' and 'receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term'. That is a direct contradiction and a dangling mechanic that a vendor could use to argue Customer's Deliverable rights expire with the Order Form term.
Fix: delete or conform the residual licence sentence (e.g. strike it, or recast as 'Vendor receives no licence to Deliverables except as expressly agreed'), which is still a short, minimal change.
Fallback is independently incomplete (revocable, term-limited, non-sublicensable Deliverable licence), so the drafter cannot fall back on that bargain if the ownership flip is resisted.
